A rectangle with side lengths $1{ }$ and $3,$ a square with side length $1,$ and a rectangle $R$ are inscribed inside a larger square as shown. The sum of all possible values for the area of $R$ can be written in the form $\frac{m}{n}$, where $m$ and $n$ are relatively prime positive integers. What is $m+n?$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The outside in the figure is a large axis-parallel square. In the upper left there is a tilted small square with side length 1, which simultaneously touches the left side and the upper side of the large square; below there is a tilted 1×3 rectangle, whose upper long side extends from near the left side to the right side, and whose lower side near it touches the bottom side of the large square; in the upper right there is rectangle R, whose left side connects the lower-right vertex of the small square and a point on the upper long side of the lower 1×3 rectangle, and R also touches the upper side and right side of the large square. Establish a coordinate system according to the specified method: let the upper-left corner of the large square be (0,0), the side length be S, the x-axis point to the right, and the y-axis point downward. Let L be the common vertex of the unit square and the 1×3 rectangle, C be the common vertex of the unit square and R, and Q be the lower-left vertex of R and lie on the upper long side of the lower 1×3 rectangle. Let the lower-side vector of the unit square be u=(a,-b), so a^2+b^2=1. Since the unit square touches the left side and upper side of the large square, we may take L=(b,a+b), C=(a+b,a). Let the long-direction unit vector of the lower 1×3 rectangle be v=(c,d), and the width direction be (-d,c). Its lower-left corner is on the left side of the large square, so d=b. Its upper-right corner is on the right side of the large square, and its lower-right corner is on the bottom side of the large square, therefore S=b+3c, and S=a+b+3d+c. Also c^2+d^2=1, a^2+b^2=1, so c=a. Substitute into the S equations and use d=b, obtaining b+3a=a+b+3b+a, therefore a=3b. From a^2+b^2=1, get a=3/sqrt(10), b=1/sqrt(10), and thus S=b+3a=sqrt(10). Let Q=L+t v, where 0<t<3. Because v=(a,b), Q=(b+ta,a+b+tb). Thus the left-side vector of R is w=Q-C=((t-1)a,(t+1)b). Take the perpendicular direction r=((t+1)b,-(t-1)a). The same multiple μr reaches the upper side of the large square from C and reaches the right side of the large square from Q, so it satisfies C_y+μr_y=0 and Q_x+μr_x=S. From C_y+μr_y=0, get a-μ(t-1)a=0, so μ=1/(t-1). Then from Q_x+μr_x=S, substituting a=3/sqrt(10), b=1/sqrt(10), get (1+3t)/sqrt(10)+(t+1)/((t-1)sqrt(10))=sqrt(10), namely 3t+(t+1)/(t-1)=9. Rearranging gives 3t^2-11t+10=0, so t=2 or t=5/3. The area of R is μ||w||^2=[9(t-1)^2+(t+1)^2]/[10(t-1)]. When t=2, the area is 9/5; when t=5/3, the area is 5/3. The sum of all possible areas is 9/5+5/3=52/15. Therefore m=52, n=15, m+n=67.

method.method_draft: Use full Cartesian coordinates. Read the outer square as axis-aligned with top-left corner at (0,0), side length S, x right and y down. From the image, let L be the common vertex of the unit square and the 1-by-3 lower rectangle, C the common vertex of the unit square and R, and Q the lower-left vertex of R lying on the long upper side of the lower 1-by-3 rectangle. Let the lower side of the upper unit square be u=(a,-b), so a^2+b^2=1; because the unit square also touches the left and top sides of the large square, L=(b,a+b) and C=(a+b,a). Let the long direction of the lower 1-by-3 rectangle be v=(c,d), and its width direction be (-d,c). Since its lower-left corner is on the left side, d=b; since its upper-right corner is on the right side and its lower-right corner is on the bottom side, S=b+3c and S=a+b+3d+c. Together with c^2+d^2=1 and a^2+b^2=1, this gives c=a and a=3b, hence a=3/sqrt(10), b=1/sqrt(10), S=sqrt(10). Now write Q=L+t v for 0<t<3. The left side of R is w=Q-C=((t-1)a,(t+1)b). A perpendicular side direction is r=((t+1)b,-(t-1)a). Since the same multiple μr takes C to the top side and Q to the right side, impose C_y+μr_y=0 and Q_x+μr_x=S. The first gives μ=1/(t-1), and the second gives 3t+(t+1)/(t-1)=9, i.e. 3t^2-11t+10=0. Solve t=2 or t=5/3. For each root, area(R)=μ||w||^2=[9(t-1)^2+(t+1)^2]/[10(t-1)]. The two areas are 9/5 and 5/3, so their sum is 52/15 and m+n=67.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中外部是一个轴平行的大正方形。左上方有一个倾斜的边长为 1 的小正方形，它同时接触大正方形的左边和上边；下方有一个倾斜的 1×3 长方形，它的上长边从左侧附近延伸到右侧，底边附近接触大正方形底边；右上方有长方形 R，它的左边连接小正方形的右下顶点和下方 1×3 长方形上长边上的一点，并且 R 还接触大正方形的上边和右边。

按指定方法建立坐标系：令大正方形左上角为 (0,0)，边长为 S，x 轴向右，y 轴向下。设 L 为单位正方形和 1×3 长方形的公共顶点，C 为单位正方形和 R 的公共顶点，Q 为 R 的左下顶点且在下方 1×3 长方形的上长边上。

设单位正方形下边向量为 u=(a,-b)，所以 a^2+b^2=1。由单位正方形接触大正方形左边和上边，可取 L=(b,a+b)，C=(a+b,a)。

设下方 1×3 长方形的长方向单位向量为 v=(c,d)，宽方向为 (-d,c)。它的左下角在大正方形左边，所以 d=b。它的右上角在大正方形右边、右下角在大正方形底边，因此 S=b+3c，且 S=a+b+3d+c。又 c^2+d^2=1，a^2+b^2=1，所以 c=a。代入 S 等式并用 d=b，得 b+3a=a+b+3b+a，因此 a=3b。由 a^2+b^2=1，得到 a=3/sqrt(10)，b=1/sqrt(10)，从而 S=b+3a=sqrt(10)。

令 Q=L+t v，其中 0<t<3。因为 v=(a,b)，所以 Q=(b+ta,a+b+tb)。于是 R 的左边向量为 w=Q-C=((t-1)a,(t+1)b)。取垂直方向 r=((t+1)b,-(t-1)a)。同一倍数 μr 从 C 到达大正方形上边，并从 Q 到达大正方形右边，因此满足 C_y+μr_y=0 和 Q_x+μr_x=S。

由 C_y+μr_y=0 得 a-μ(t-1)a=0，所以 μ=1/(t-1)。再由 Q_x+μr_x=S，代入 a=3/sqrt(10)，b=1/sqrt(10)，得到 (1+3t)/sqrt(10)+(t+1)/((t-1)sqrt(10))=sqrt(10)，即 3t+(t+1)/(t-1)=9。整理得 3t^2-11t+10=0，所以 t=2 或 t=5/3。

R 的面积为 μ||w||^2=[9(t-1)^2+(t+1)^2]/[10(t-1)]。当 t=2 时，面积为 9/5；当 t=5/3 时，面积为 5/3。所有可能面积之和为 9/5+5/3=52/15。因此 m=52，n=15，m+n=67。

method.method_draft: Use projection lengths and avoid fixed point coordinates. From the image, define p as the horizontal projection and q as the vertical projection of the relevant unit side of the tilted unit square, so p^2+q^2=1. The upper unit square touches the left and top sides, so the shared vertex L is q units from the left edge and p+q units below the top edge. For the lower 1-by-3 rectangle, let its long side have projection 3p horizontally and 3q vertically, and its width have projections q horizontally and p vertically; the image shows that its width reaches the left side from L, while its long side reaches the right side and its far width corner reaches the bottom side. Therefore the side length S of the outer square can be computed two ways: S=q+3p from the right-side contact and S=(p+q)+3q+p=2p+4q from the bottom contact. Hence q+3p=2p+4q, so p=3q, and with p^2+q^2=1 we get p=3/sqrt(10), q=1/sqrt(10). Now let Q be t units from L along the long side of the lower rectangle, where Q is the lower-left vertex of R shown on that side. The segment CQ has horizontal projection (t-1)p and vertical projection (t+1)q. The adjacent side of R is perpendicular, so before scaling its horizontal/vertical projections are (t+1)q and (t-1)p. If the scale factor is k, reaching the top side from C gives k(t-1)p=p, so k=1/(t-1). Reaching the right side from Q gives q+tp+k(t+1)q=q+3p. Substitute p=3q to get 3t+(t+1)/(t-1)=9, or 3t^2-11t+10=0. Instead of treating the roots separately, use Vieta: the roots have sum 11/3 and product 10/3. The area for a root t is A(t)=(((t-1)p)^2+((t+1)q)^2)/(t-1)=[9(t-1)^2+(t+1)^2]/[10(t-1)]. Sum A(t) over the two roots using Vieta to get 52/15, so m+n=67.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中有一个大正方形。左上方有一个倾斜的边长为 1 的小正方形，它同时接触大正方形的左边和上边。下方有一个倾斜的 1×3 矩形，它的一个宽边从左上附近的公共点延到大正方形左边，长边向右下方延伸并接触右边，另一个角接触底边。右上方有矩形 R，它的左下角落在下方 1×3 矩形的上长边上，并且 R 接触大正方形的上边和右边。

raw_record.original_question: A rectangle with side lengths $1$ and $3$, a square with side length $1$, and a rectangle $R$ are inscribed inside a larger square as shown. The sum of all possible values for the area of $R$ can be written in the form $\frac{m}{n}$, where $m$ and $n$ are relatively prime positive integers. What is $m+n$?
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The outside in the figure is a large axis-parallel square. In the upper left there is a tilted small square with side length 1, which simultaneously touches the left side and the upper side of the large square; below there is a tilted 1×3 rectangle, whose upper long side extends from near the left side to the right side, and whose lower side near it touches the bottom side of the large square; in the upper right there is rectangle R, whose left side connects the lower-right vertex of the small square and a point on the upper long side of the lower 1×3 rectangle, and R also touches the upper side and right side of the large square.

Establish a coordinate system according to the specified method: let the upper-left corner of the large square be (0,0), the side length be S, the x-axis point to the right, and the y-axis point downward. Let L be the common vertex of the unit square and the 1×3 rectangle, C be the common vertex of the unit square and R, and Q be the lower-left vertex of R and lie on the upper long side of the lower 1×3 rectangle.

Let the lower-side vector of the unit square be u=(a,-b), so a^2+b^2=1. Since the unit square touches the left side and upper side of the large square, we may take L=(b,a+b), C=(a+b,a).

Let the long-direction unit vector of the lower 1×3 rectangle be v=(c,d), and the width direction be (-d,c). Its lower-left corner is on the left side of the large square, so d=b. Its upper-right corner is on the right side of the large square, and its lower-right corner is on the bottom side of the large square, therefore S=b+3c, and S=a+b+3d+c. Also c^2+d^2=1, a^2+b^2=1, so c=a. Substitute into the S equations and use d=b, obtaining b+3a=a+b+3b+a, therefore a=3b. From a^2+b^2=1, get a=3/sqrt(10), b=1/sqrt(10), and thus S=b+3a=sqrt(10).

Let Q=L+t v, where 0<t<3. Because v=(a,b), Q=(b+ta,a+b+tb). Thus the left-side vector of R is w=Q-C=((t-1)a,(t+1)b). Take the perpendicular direction r=((t+1)b,-(t-1)a). The same multiple μr reaches the upper side of the large square from C and reaches the right side of the large square from Q, so it satisfies C_y+μr_y=0 and Q_x+μr_x=S.

From C_y+μr_y=0, get a-μ(t-1)a=0, so μ=1/(t-1). Then from Q_x+μr_x=S, substituting a=3/sqrt(10), b=1/sqrt(10), get (1+3t)/sqrt(10)+(t+1)/((t-1)sqrt(10))=sqrt(10), namely 3t+(t+1)/(t-1)=9. Rearranging gives 3t^2-11t+10=0, so t=2 or t=5/3.

The area of R is μ||w||^2=[9(t-1)^2+(t+1)^2]/[10(t-1)]. When t=2, the area is 9/5; when t=5/3, the area is 5/3. The sum of all possible areas is 9/5+5/3=52/15. Therefore m=52, n=15, m+n=67.
